answer: Each worker binds its signing key to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is locked before it can vote on jobs. A kernel of randomly selected peers checks the work, while an echo round asks independently sampled agents to reproduce its result; agreement counts only when their keys trace to distinct stake deposits. The deposit acts as an anchor for one accountable identity, so splitting into many fake agents requires buying and locking more capital, which risks slashing if those agents collude or submit bad work.
